hypothesis: On the six fixed synthetic block-polynomial residuals, all certified budgets contain independently evaluated block norms. At least one of the three core fixtures meets its fixed tolerance under the complete constant-two ellipse budget while none of the implemented applicable older functional-calculus budgets certifies it. Stronger prior special cases receive zero incremental credit. A direct block-norm certificate is separately reported as an older exact method; a functional-calculus budget win is not a claim of faster or better practical certification than direct calculation.
parent_plan_limits: This executable finite synthetic audit operationalizes the pending budget hypothesis. It cannot establish that every older mathematical certificate was exhausted, a new theorem, or practical savings over exact direct norms. input.kind: explicit synthetic coupled-channel polynomial residual budget; no real application dataset or training workload
input.exposure: Both source manuscripts and selected old statements were read before registration. No fixture norm, supremum or tolerance decision has been calculated. This is not blind theorem discovery.
input.matrix_rule: Real A=diag(diagonal)+K. Each [i,j,w] adds K_ij=w,K_ji=-w; unspecified entries zero. Preserve listed indices and rational numbers exactly.
input.coefficient_rule: R(z)=B0+z B1+z^2 B2, with real rational coefficient matrices. Base-first tensor evaluation R[A]=I tensor B0+A tensor B1+A^2 tensor B2. These are frozen residuals, not results of a fitted approximator.
input.ellipse_enclosure: Let h=max|diagonal| and k=max_i sum_j |K_ij|. For k>0 the numerical range lies in [-h,h]+i[-k,k], inside the ellipse with semiaxes X=5h/4,Y=5k/3 because (h/X)^2+(k/Y)^2=1. X>Y is required. Exterior map z=a w+b/w,a=(X+Y)/2,b=(X-Y)/2. For k=0 use the segment and direct diagonal old control instead of a degenerate exterior ellipse.
input.boundary_grid: Four quarter-circle rational parametrizations w=i^j*((1-t^2)+2it)/(1+t^2),j=0..3,t=l/64,l=0..64. All values and squared singular values use rational arithmetic and dyadic square-root enclosures,not floating-point trig.
input.supremum_certificate: For R degree2 on a disk radius X, L=||B1||+2X||B2|| bounds ||R(z)-R(z')||/|z-z'|. Ellipse/circle parametrization speed<=2X, so every parameter point is within1/(2*64) of a sampled parameter and the global maximum is <=max_sample_upper+L*X/64. Maximum principle for matrix operator norm places the interior maximum on the boundary. Record the full additive correction;sample maximum alone is not a certificate. For the normal segment use the exact spectral points for the prior constant-one certificate.
input.norm_arithmetic: For complex rational 1x1/2x2 coefficient evaluations, singular norm is enclosed via the exact Gram trace/determinant quadratic and outward dyadic square roots. Real block norms are independently bracketed by rational positive-definiteness bisection of lambda I-M^T M using exact elimination;the initial lambda upper bound is1+max absolute Gram row sum. Strict PD failure gives a valid non-strict lower spectral bound. Return exact rational interval endpoints.

baseline.weak_general: Complete(1+sqrt2) times exactly the same certified ellipse supremum upper bound,using an outward rational sqrt2 interval.
baseline.faber: Old scalar Faber norm<=2 extends to the block triangle bound. For ellipse z=a w+b/w,F1=z/a,F2=(z/a)^2-2b/a;R=C0+F1 C1+F2 C2 with C0=B0+2ab B2,C1=a B1,C2=a^2 B2. Old budget ||C0||+2||C1||+2||C2|| uses outward coefficient norm enclosures. Verify this polynomial coefficient identity exactly.
baseline.disk: The ellipse lies in |z|<=X. Old complete disk constant2 gives twice its certified matrix-polynomial circle supremum,using exactly the same64-grid and Lipschitz correction.
baseline.special: Scalar coefficients and base<=3 already have prior constant2 on the same enclosure,so they cannot count as new benefit. Normal A uses the spectral theorem and exact maximum over listed diagonal eigenvalues,constant1.
baseline.direct: The independently certified direct block norm is an older exact alternative and is reported for every fixture. No win against this direct certificate or large-scale cost advantage is inferred. Other older certificates not implemented are an explicit residual gap.

judge: Construct R[A] twice: base-first Kronecker powers, and coefficient-block entrywise Horner evaluation followed by the explicit tensor-order permutation. Require exact matrix agreement. Enclose its norm with rational Gram-matrix PD bisection. Check the ellipse containment algebra,coefficient commutators,normality,exact Faber identity,all upper budgets and prior-scope controls. Use deterministic arithmetic only;no statistical extrapolation.

success.tolerance_is_fixed: 1/4 for every case;do not replace after results

failure: Any invalid enclosure,block evaluation mismatch,uncertified norm/supremum,failed fixed control,resource violation,or absence of at least one core decision improvement after the implemented strong old baselines. Preserve outputs and classify an unfavorable prediction as observation pending humans,not formal rejection. Unimplemented old certificates prevent a universal novelty claim even if the finite criterion passes.
